pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/104350
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/104337
This PR adds NAOT/R2R support for https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/103361

Example:
```cs
static int Test1()
{
    MyClass obj = new MyClass(42); // MyClass allocation never escapes
    return obj.X;
}

static int Test2()
{
    object o = 42; // boxing (allocation)
    return (int)o; // unboxing
}

public class MyClass(int x)
{
    public int X => x;
}
```
Old codegen for `Test()` on NAOT (and R2R):
```asm
; Assembly listing for method Proga:Test1():int (FullOpts)
; NativeAOT compilation
       sub      rsp, 40
       lea      rcx, [(reloc 0x40000000004211a8)]      ; MyClass
       call     CORINFO_HELP_NEWSFAST
       mov      dword ptr [rax+0x08], 42
       mov      eax, dword ptr [rax+0x08]
       add      rsp, 40
       ret

; Assembly listing for method Proga:Test2():int (FullOpts)
; NativeAOT compilation
       sub      rsp, 40
       lea      rcx, [(reloc 0x4000000000421008)]      ; Int32
       call     CORINFO_HELP_NEWSFAST
       mov      dword ptr [rax+0x08], 42
       mov      eax, dword ptr [rax+0x08]
       add      rsp, 40
       ret
```
New codegen:
```asm
; Assembly listing for method Proga:Test1():int (FullOpts)
; NativeAOT compilation
       mov      eax, 42
       ret      

; Assembly listing for method Proga:Test2():int (FullOpts)
; NativeAOT compilation
       mov      eax, 42
       ret      
```

> Looks good to me. [dotnet/coreclr@323d3b3](https://github.com/dotnet/coreclr/commit/323d3b37545b3918014055efb714fa4f16ecdc0e) had one more adjustment when computing the GC pointer map to account for the extra MethodTable field. I assume we don't have an off-by-one bug in GC reporting and/or there's a targeted GC test to ensure the GC reporting is not bogus?

@MichalStrehovsky I don't think we have a test checking GC info explicitly, I'd expect it to fail badly if it was miscomputing GC info map here. I've just made some tests to check it, e.g. for a class like this:
```cs
public record MyClass(long A, string B, MyStruct MS);

// Nested struct field
public record struct MyStruct(int C, string D);
```
the `byte* gcPtr` we get from `GatherClassGCLayout` is `00-01-00-01-00` (the result of `BitConverter.ToString(gcPtr)`) which translates into:
```
8 bytes - pMT pointer
8 bytes - string (GC pointer!)
8 bytes - long
8 bytes - string (GC pointer!)
8 bytes - int + 4b padding
-----------------
40 bytes
```
_NOTE: some fields were re-ordered by auto-layout_
so looks like everything is correct, we don't need to add any explicit pMT offset like Eugene did in that commit for CoreCLR, because `field.Offset.AsInt` already does what we need.

review_comments:
`getHeapClassSize` has `Debug.Assert(_compilation.IsInheritanceChainLayoutFixedInCurrentVersionBubble(type));` assert. What guarantees that this assert is satisfied?

The stack allocation should be disabled for non-valuetype types that are not fixed in the current version bubble. How is it achieved?

@jkotas it's checked via a separate JIT-EE API: [canAllocateOnStack](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/041375910885f3a30ccf0bb8b751566dae7043f4/src/coreclr/tools/Common/JitInterface/CorInfoImpl.cs#L2163-L2166) so JIT will never call this function if `canAllocateOnStack` returned false.

This was copied from CoreCLR impl, it does a similar memset (see [this](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/c52177b21cb358d45a18a1f14d5855aedb61d0ec/src/coreclr/vm/jitinterface.cpp#L2422-L2425))

Previously, `getClassGClayout` used `InstanceFieldSize.AsInt` which for ref types always return just pointer-size while we need the real size. Since it has never been used for ref-types before, it wasn't an issue.

> What's the problem with MethodTable*?

Afair, they're in different namespaces in CoreCLR and NAOT, is it important to keep it MethodTable* ?
